A regular maintenance program would be set up for the Bad Creek Pumped Storage Plant. Equipment inspection and analysis of collected data would determine when overhaul would be necessary. Any leakage through the dams and movement of the dams would be monitored. During the scheduled outage period, the turbine runner and wicket gates would be inspected for cavitation. These programs would be maintained during the life of the project.
The FPC Staff inspects all licensed projects to ensure their physical safety and the safety of the public, and to observe compliance with articles of the license. Proposed project sites are inspected during early planning stages to review the adequacy of the Applicant's investigations and to identify potential problem areas. Licenses for new major hydroelectric projects require the licensee to engage a board of qualified engineering consultants to review design and construction to assure that the project, as designed, will be safe and adequate. These boards would convene periodically, with special meetings as required at critical construction stages, such as foundation excavation, placement of fill materials, and special problem areas. Licensees are also required to submit prior to construction their construction inspection programs for approval. Projects under construction would be inspected at least monthly by Commission Staff, with possibly more frequent visits during critical construction stages, to ensure that construction is in accordance with approved license exhibits and terms of the license, and that acceptable engineering practices are being employed. The project in operation would be inspected annually, or more often if deemed necessary, to assure that it is maintained and operated efficiently and safely and in compliance with the license. Safety features such as spillway gates and other control structures would be carefully examined. Special problem areas would be observed and recommendations made, if needed, and a review would also be made of instrumentation data monitored and collected by the licensee for such things as seepage, settlement, and deflections.
Part 12 of the Commission's Regulations under the Federal Power Act requires licensees to have operating projects inspected at least once every five years by qualified independent engineering consultants. These inspections require a visual examination of all structures and equipment, an analysis of any instrumentation data collected, a review of the stability of the structures, the spillway capacity, and the affects of overtopping of the structures.
